### Licence texts

MIT and BSD require their text and the copyright notice to travel with a binary. The notice is
the **Copyright** column above; the text is below, each distinct text once. A package whose own
licence file differs from the standard text has a block of its own.

### Native libraries inside SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp

The SkiaSharp and HarfBuzzSharp packages are MIT, but the native libraries they carry
(`libSkiaSharp.dll`, `libHarfBuzzSharp.dll`) are other projects' code under their own licences.
These two notices are taken verbatim from the `THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt` in the native-assets
packages; that file also names the libraries inside Skia (FreeType, libpng, libjpeg-turbo, zlib,
ICU and others) and ships whole in `licenses/` beside this file.

modifies fourteen of them. They are, with what was changed and why:

Those changes are committed on the `uetoolkit-patches` branch of the local CUE4Parse checkout, so
the list above can be regenerated rather than trusted:

```bash
git -C ../FModel-dev/CUE4Parse diff --stat cc79bf64 uetoolkit-patches
```

### Inside CUE4Parse-Natives.dll — ACL and RTM, MIT

`CUE4Parse-Natives.dll` is compiled from source, not taken from NuGet, so tools/notice.ps1 cannot see
what is inside it. It statically links the **Animation Compression Library** twice (the 2.x decoder
CUE4Parse uses, and the vendored 1.3.5 decoder beside it, `acl1`) and **Realtime Math**, which ACL
is built on. All three are MIT, and the MIT licence requires its text and the copyright line to
travel with a binary:

- Animation Compression Library — https://github.com/nfrechette/acl —
  Copyright (c) 2017 Nicholas Frechette & Animation Compression Library contributors
- Realtime Math — https://github.com/nfrechette/rtm — Copyright (c) 2018 Nicholas Frechette

The MIT licence text they use is the "MIT" text under "Licence texts" above.

### The ones with obligations beyond attribution

**Six Labors ImageSharp** ships under the Six Labors Split License, not a plain open-source
licence. Its Apache-2.0 terms apply here on two independent grounds, either of which is enough:
it arrives as a TRANSITIVE dependency (through CUE4Parse, never referenced directly), and this
project is the work of an individual under the revenue threshold that licence names. If either of
those ever stops being true, read that licence again before shipping.

**Oodle.NET and OodleSharp** are MIT WRAPPERS and are not the proprietary compressor. See
"Deliberately NOT bundled" below, which is about `oo2core` itself.

---

## Deliberately NOT bundled

**Oodle** (`oo2core`) is proprietary compression technology owned by Epic Games / RAD Game Tools.
It is **downloaded at runtime** by `ProviderFactory.InitNativesAsync` and is never redistributed by
this project. That is not an accident of implementation — shipping it would be a licensing problem,
and the runtime download is the same approach FModel takes. Do not "simplify" this by copying the
DLL into the release.

**Detex** is likewise fetched at runtime rather than bundled.

## Still to decide

1. ~~The licence for this project's own code.~~ **Decided 2026-09-11: GPL-3.0**, from version
   1.6.0 onward. Earlier releases shipped under a proprietary "free to use, do not redistribute"
   licence and keep the terms they were downloaded under; nobody's rights shrink, because GPL-3.0
   grants strictly more than that did.

   The reasoning, so it is not re-litigated. An OSI licence had been rejected once, and the
   objection was specific: **MIT would let anyone redistribute and relicense**, which is the
   opposite of the point. GPL-3.0 answers exactly that — relicensing is the one thing it forbids.
   Forks are welcome and need no permission; what a fork may not do is close itself.

   Against the two things actually feared:

   - **Somebody putting their own name on it** — forbidden. Copyright notices must be preserved
     and changes marked.
   - **Somebody putting it behind a paywall** — *not* forbidden. The GPL permits charging. But
     every buyer may demand the source and redistribute it freely, so the model collapses rather
     than being illegal. Forbidding it outright would need a non-commercial licence, which is not
     open source and would partly reopen the "closed system" criticism this answers.

   Apache-2.0 (CUE4Parse) combines one-way into GPL-3.0. The component above that needs more
   than attribution — **ImageSharp** (Six Labors Split License) — is unchanged by this and is
   already worked through in its own section.

2. ~~Whether a `.usmap` may be redistributed.~~ **Decided: we ship one.**

   `UEToolkit.App/mappings/` carries a usmap dumped from Star Wars Zero Company — the property
   layout of that game's classes, derived from the shipped build. The basis for shipping it is
   community practice: usmaps are shared openly and routinely, including in FModel's own Discord,
   and nobody treats this as contentious.

   Two things are worth knowing rather than re-deriving later.

   FModel itself does **not** bundle usmaps; it asks the user to supply one. That may simply be
   because it supports hundreds of games, so this is weak evidence either way — but it is the
   closest comparable project, and it made the other choice.

   **The decision is reversible by deleting the folder, and nothing depends on the folder
   existing.** Measured, not assumed: with `mappings/` removed, `--addgame` falls back to
   `"UE5 needs a .usmap - set it in Game Settings"`, which is exactly FModel's behaviour. What it
   ALSO loses is the engine version — `GameInstall.EngineFromMappings` reads `-5.6.1-` out of the
   filename, and without it the guess drops to `GAME_UE5_5`, which is wrong for this game and
   wrong in the silent way (it mounts, it indexes, it reads meshes wrong). So the usmap is doing
   two jobs, and dropping it costs both.

3. **Where the CUE4Parse fork lives.** The patches above exist only on a local branch, on a clone
   whose `origin` is upstream. Pushing them to a fork under an account we control is what makes
   this project buildable by anyone else — and is also what makes the modification notice above
   verifiable rather than a claim.
